scenario.summary: A Mallox ransomware affiliate gained access to internet-facing MS-SQL servers by brute-forcing the 'sa' account. Once inside, they leveraged SQL features like xp_cmdshell and CLR assemblies to stage a PowerShell script that deployed the PureCrypter loader, which ultimately executed the Mallox ransomware payload while attempting to evade detection through sandbox checks and security tool patching.

meta.rationale: The hunt scopes to all hosts with SQL Server components. If specific IP ranges or cloud instances are known to be public-facing, analysts should filter the brute-force leads to focus on those first.
meta.hypothesis: An adversary is targeting publicly exposed SQL Servers with high-frequency 'sa' account brute-force attempts to execute OS-level commands via database shell breakouts like xp_cmdshell or OLE automation.

hunt.name: Mallox: SQL Server Brute-Force to OS Breakout
hunt.description: This hunt identifies the early stages of a Mallox ransomware infection. It focuses on identifying high-volume authentication failures against the Microsoft SQL 'sa' account followed by anomalous process execution where the SQL Server service (sqlservr.exe) acts as a parent to system shells or administrative tools. By combining brute-force telemetry from sign-in logs with parent-child process baselining on the endpoint, we can detect affiliates attempting to break out of the database context to deploy PureCrypter loaders.

config.content: SELECT DISTINCT device_hostname FROM hb_software_inventory WHERE (LOWER(package_name) LIKE '%sql server%' OR LOWER(vendor_name) LIKE '%microsoft%sql%') AND asset_scope = 'endpoint'
config.description: Scope the hunt to hosts running Microsoft SQL Server based on installed software inventory.
config.expected_signal: A list of hostnames known to have SQL Server installed. Silence means no SQL Servers are in the inventory.

primitive_config.label: Identify SQL Server Hosts
primitive_config.content: SELECT DISTINCT device_hostname FROM hb_software_inventory WHERE (LOWER(package_name) LIKE '%sql server%' OR LOWER(vendor_name) LIKE '%microsoft%sql%') AND asset_scope = 'endpoint'
primitive_config.expected: A list of hostnames known to have SQL Server installed. Silence means no SQL Servers are in the inventory.

config.content: SELECT dst_endpoint_name, src_endpoint_ip, COUNT(*) as fail_count, MIN(time) as first_seen, MAX(time) as last_seen FROM hb_auth_signin WHERE LOWER(actor_user_name) = 'sa' AND status_id = 2 AND activity_id = 5 AND time >= datetime('now', '-{{lookback_days}} days') GROUP BY dst_endpoint_name, src_endpoint_ip HAVING fail_count >= {{min_attempts}} ORDER BY fail_count DESC
config.description: Identify external or internal sources targeting the 'sa' account with high-frequency failures.
config.expected_signal: IPs targeting the 'sa' account on specific service endpoints. Silence indicates no high-volume brute force in the window.

config.content: SELECT device_hostname, process_name, process_cmd_line, parent_process_name, user_name, time FROM hb_process_activity WHERE LOWER(parent_process_name) LIKE '%sqlservr.exe%' AND (LOWER(process_name) LIKE '%cmd.exe%' OR LOWER(process_name) LIKE '%powershell.exe%' OR LOWER(process_name) LIKE '%wmic.exe%' OR LOWER(process_name) LIKE '%wscript.exe%' OR LOWER(process_name) LIKE '%scrcons.exe%') AND time >= datetime('now', '-{{lookback_days}} days')
config.description: Find instances where the SQL service process is the parent of an OS shell, suggesting exploitation of xp_cmdshell.
config.expected_signal: OS shells spawned by the SQL engine. This is a high-fidelity indicator of a breakout.

config.content: SELECT LOWER(process_name) AS child_path, COUNT(DISTINCT device_hostname) AS host_count, COUNT(*) as total_runs, MIN(time) as first_seen FROM hb_process_activity WHERE LOWER(parent_process_name) LIKE '%sqlservr.exe%' AND time >= datetime('now', '-{{lookback_days}} days') GROUP BY child_path HAVING host_count <= 2 ORDER BY host_count ASC
config.description: Stack-count children of sqlservr.exe to identify rare binaries that may be dropped loaders or custom assemblies.
config.expected_signal: A binary spawned by SQL Server that appears on only one or two hosts in the fleet.
